questions.question: The three measuring points on the circular flow's one pipe are:
options: PRODUCTION, INCOME and SPENDING — three gauges that must in principle agree

questions.question: GDP is defined as:
options: All money spent by government in a year
The total market value of all FINAL goods and services produced WITHIN a country's borders in a given period
The income of a country's citizens worldwide
The total of all sales including intermediate goods

questions.question: "Market value" appears in the definition because:
options: Prices let unlike things — haircuts and coal — be added into one total

questions.question: GDP is measured as:
options: A stockpile of everything ever produced
A FLOW per period — usually one year, reported quarterly

subtopics.title: GDP's Fine Print — Final Goods and the Border

questions.question: Wheat R4 → flour R7 → loaf R18. GDP counts:
options: R18 only (or the value added: 4 + 3 + 11) — intermediate goods are already inside the loaf's price

questions.question: A foreign-owned mine on South African soil counts in:
options: SOUTH AFRICAN GDP — geography decides, not nationality

questions.question: Uncle reselling his old bakkie is excluded because:
options: It was counted when new — reselling changes ownership without new production (though a dealer's service fee is new and counts)

questions.question: Social grants are excluded from GDP because:
options: They are too hard to measure
They are TRANSFERS — money moved without payment for production

questions.question: The one thing GNI changes from GDP is:
options: The rule of belonging — WHO earned the income (residents' factors, wherever producing) instead of WHERE it was produced

questions.question: The bridge from GDP to GNI:
options: Add all exports, subtract all imports
SUBTRACT factor income paid to foreign owners; ADD factor income residents earn abroad

questions.question: South Africa's GNI runs somewhat below its GDP because:
options: Substantial foreign ownership means more factor income LEAVES than arrives — the machine here produces more than residents keep

questions.question: Lesotho can show GNI ABOVE GDP because:
options: Many citizens work abroad and remit wages — its people earn more than its territory produces

subtopics.title: Per Capita, Comparisons and the Limits of the Number

questions.question: Per capita GDP is:
options: GDP divided by population — output per person, the first correction for welfare comparisons
GDP divided by the number of firms

questions.question: Comparing GDP across years also requires:
options: Stripping out the inflation effect — a bigger number is not better if prices simply rose

questions.question: "One billionaire and ninety-nine unemployed average out respectably" exposes GDP's silence on:
options: DISTRIBUTION — the number says nothing about who holds the income

questions.question: "A speedometer, not a report card" means GDP:
options: Is essential for what it reads — production and growth — and silent on health, fairness, unpaid work and the environment

questions.question: The mechanic's R300 parts and R900 repair enter the count as:
options: R900 (or the mechanic's added R600 on top of the parts' R300) — never R1 200

questions.question: Granny's grant and uncle's bakkie resale share the feature that:
options: Money MOVED without anything new being made — the count wants only the new

questions.question: The outsider-owned shop on the street counts in the street's GDP because:
options: It stands here, employs here, produces here — the border rule, street-sized

questions.question: The street's daughter working in Sandton counts:
options: In GNI (she is ours; her earnings come home) but NOT in the street's GDP (her work happens there)

questions.question: GDP measures the street as:
options: A MACHINE — how much this place, as a place, produces

questions.question: "The machine is here, the keeping is elsewhere" describes:
options: Roughly South Africa's shape — big GDP, smaller GNI, profits of foreign-owned firms riding out

questions.question: The real story between GDP and GNI is told by:
options: Whichever number is larger being the true one
The GAP between them — reading it reveals the economy's ownership and labour structure

subtopics.title: What the Big Number Can't See

questions.question: The grandmother minding four children daily is:
options: Enormous value with no receipt — uncounted, so the official number undersells streets like ours
Counted in GDP as childcare services

questions.question: Selling the big tree for timber makes the count:
options: Go UP — while the tree's absence appears nowhere: production that eats tomorrow looks identical to production that doesn't

questions.question: "A street can produce more and live worse" exposes the blind spot of:
options: WELL-BEING — the count sees sales, not safety, health or learning

questions.question: The balanced final reading of GDP is:
options: The number is the whole truth
The number matters — growth funds wages and clinics — AND it is a speedometer, not a report card: how fast, never how well, and never for whom
